title.narrative: COVID-19: Supporting Post-COVID-19 Small-Scale Employment Creation

description.narrative: With the onset of the COVID-19 pandemic, government's efforts took on increased urgency and many short-term measures were put in place to provide immediate support for social protection and job protection. While most of the social protection measures were through direct cash or in-kind transfer and expansion of welfare programs, the support for industry and job protection will mostly be carried out through credit lines and liquidity support through financial sector. The total amount of credit lines, refinance programs, and credit protection schemes announced, has reached Tk1 trillion. But the retrenchment of the financial sector and capacity constraints present a challenge to deliver the funds timely and efficiently especially to reach certain highly vulnerable sectors.

By December 2025, at least 45,000 employment opportunities created among the beneficiaries of the program. The PMU, with the help of the TA consultants, has initiated another survey activity during the last quarter of 2025, to evaluate employment creation for the subsequent period from October 2024 to December 2025. Output: Financial support to enterprises started or operated by migrants, rural enterprises, and youth from the formal banking sector increased Indicator: By June 2025, 30,000 returning migrants, unemployed youth, and rural micro and small business owners (20% women) supported with financing Progress/Status: As of December 2025, 31,082 borrowers have been supported with financing through the PFIs, comprising 6,395 rural entrepreneurs, 24,189 unemployed youth, and 498 returning migrants. Of the 31,082 borrowers, 11,487 (36.96%) are rural women entrepreneurs. Data Source: Executing agency report, project periodical monitoring reports, banks' annual reports Actual value:

Output: Action plan for promoting formal banking sector support for cottage, micro, and small enterprises developed Indicator: By December 2024, at least 200 women entrepreneurs are supported by incubation services Progress/Status: The TA successfully completed this activity by organizing eight batches of training programs in Rajshahi, Chittagong, and Dhaka in collaboration with BRAC Learning Center, Chittagong Women Chamber of Commerce and Industry (CWCCI), SME Foundation, and Bangladesh Women Chamber of Commerce and Industry (BWCCI). During these training programs, a total of 232 people were trained, 210 of them were female. These training programs were held with incubates of CWCCI (3 batches) and SME Foundation (3 batches) in their respective incubation centers, which were built by ADB via the Second Small and Medium-Sized Enterprise Development Project (SMEDP2). Furthermore, the TA project was able to form partnerships with BWCCI and RWCCI, resulting in the organization of two additional batches for those institutions' incubates.
Data Source: TA reports and final report Actual value:
